newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cerj minimum price to be published Friday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cerj minimum price to be published Friday.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state will publish on Friday the minimum price for state power firm Cerj, which is being sold off at a privatization auction November 20, a state planning official said.
The company has been valued at 700 million reais ($700 million) by the state, but a consortium led by Banco Garantia which has drawn up the privatization model for Cerj is setting the final price.

The state of Rio will also publish the percentage of the sale price which can be paid with privatization bonds, the official said. Investors will probably be able to pay 30 percent in privatization bonds and 70 percent in cash.

The rules of the privatization auction were published September 11. Under the terms, any consortium interested in buying Cerj would have to include a power company with at least 1 million customers, sales of at least 5,000 gigawatts and less than 12 percent energy losses.
Cerj employees have the right to acquire 10 percent of Cerj's share capital currently held by the state of Rio de Janeiro. The state holds 78 percent of the power firm's capital.
The remaining 70.2 percent will be sold off in one block to a consortium during a closed envelope auction.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
